There are several ways to find your wallet configuration

For Swan Vault recovery, use the descriptor from your "Wallet Configuration":

For recovery from Specter, use the "Bitcoin Core Receive Descriptor":

You can enter a receive or combined descriptor. Receive descriptors typically start with wsh or wpkh and end with /0/*; combined descriptors end with /<0;1>/*.

Automatic Change Descriptor Calculation

By default, Tempura automatically calculates the change descriptor paths ending in /1/* from your receive descriptor if the receive descriptor paths end with /0/*, which is the most common format. The same goes for multipath descriptors of type <0;1>.

Hence, you only need to enter a change descriptor if it is non-standard.

What is an Electrum Server?

An Electrum server is a special type of computer that helps you connect to the Bitcoin Network. It allows your wallet to quickly check existing balances & transactions and even broadcast new ones. Think of it as a helpful assistant that can interact with the network without requiring your computer to download the entire Bitcoin blockchain.

An internet connection is required to check your balance, existing transactions, or to broadcast a new transaction. An internet connection is not involved in the signing process.

Using your own server is easy

Enter your custom Electrum server in the format server:port. If the server uses SSL, you must specify it at the beginning.

For example: ssl://electrum.satoshi.com:50001

This is optional, and if left blank, the default server (Blockstream) will be used.

Why would I want to change my network?

Bitcoin is a network of computers. It can be scary to use, because real money is involved. For this reason, the 'Testnet' network exists. It's like a sandbox where you can play around with Bitcoin without using real money. It's also possible to create a small local network called 'Regtest' which you can control!

Developers love these features because they need to test things before releasing them, and Bitcoin is no exception.

Understanding the Fee Rate

Miners prioritize transactions based on this rate, which reflects how much is paid per "virtual byte" (a measure of transaction complexity). A higher fee rate increases the chances of a quicker confirmation, especially in periods of high network activity.

Setting a fee manually is optional. If left blank, Tempura will automatically estimate the fee rate needed to prioritize your transaction for the next block.
